analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. Its single hunk adds one table row near head line 671 describing prompt-chunk attention: 128-query blocks, a fused causal prefill path where MLX supports the head_dim, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 rollback. I examined the three base-text units (lines 808-1586) and found no changed text there. They are surrounding context only.

The patch is documentation-only, so it adds no code, endpoints, wire fields, keys or storage and weakens no control. It does not touch trust boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011. It does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache controls: salt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL, the DBK3 AAD, or the kill switch. It also does not touch the mitigations for A-001 (consumer prompts) or the provider key assets.

The row describes a performance and attention-kernel path. The fused causal call applies only to full-attention chunks with no window, softcap, vision span or bidirectional mask. The documented env knob can only restore the previous block path.

Residual question for later passes: the actual source changes in AttentionV1.swift and PagedLayerCache.swift (cited in the row) are not in this batch. A fused causal path could alter masking or cross-request isolation semantics for paged KV, or for the vision-span and bidirectional exclusions, if mis-gated. I cannot evaluate that from the supplied docs, so I make no finding. The code change should be reviewed with its own source units if it exists in the PR. This is a documentation-only conclusion, not a claim that the underlying implementation is safe.
